executiveSummary: GM0399's 2025 identity, boundary, population, neighbourhoods, settlements and safety-region inputs reconcile, and the focused deterministic gate covers all ten presets, six checkpoints and eight services. Release remains correction-required. The coastal preset reports an internal flood field of 2.552973 and 13,329 affected people-equivalent at T+24 even though no LIWO source water, defence/breach, variant, connected footprint, arrival or recession is selected for inland, protected Heiloo. Exact-zero direct Rhine/Meuse/IJssel forcing is only a narrow screen and cannot clear Egmondervaart, Hoevervaart, Baafjespolder, groundwater, sewer, regional-water or pluvial pathways. Eight nonzero hazard families reuse exactly the same complete twenty-neighbourhood ranking. A controlled fire source in Gemeentebos yields direct fire 0.654580 yet Gemeentebos ranks fourth. The three-edge road graph, station and scheduled stops do not resolve local crossings, rail state, hospital/care transfer, supplies or the A9/N203 corridors. Public drainage projects, 65 water assets, GGZ Willibrord presence, external acute care, antennas, schools and one grid-planning sample improve context but do not establish live topology, occupancy, capacity, passability, backup or restoration. Unknown and NoData must remain distinct from zero and safe; precise first-72-hour consequences remain synthetic exercise outputs until governed event-valid evidence supports them.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: GM0399 official 2025 municipality, neighbourhood and place geography and statistics
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; PDOK services inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The annual CC BY 4.0 CBS/PDOK input identifies GM0399 as Heiloo and reports 24,341 residents, density 1,301/km², 27.7% aged 65 or older and 4,025 one-person households; the generated centre is inside the 2025 boundary.

Twenty published neighbourhood rows sum to 24,355 residents, fourteen above the municipality total (+0.058%); households sum to 11,155 and rounded age-65-plus rows to 6,735. Deterministic allocation reconciles to 24,341 without rewriting observations.

One active BAG woonplaats is named Heiloo; BRT identifies Heiloo as woonkern and Kapel and Oosterzij as deelkernen. BAG/PDOK place context is Public Domain Mark 1.0 and independently updated; labels are not hydraulic compartments, sewer catchments, care footprints or event-time occupancy.

The fresh official municipality feature is MultiPolygon 2025GM0399 with 1,247 coordinate positions. CBS null, suppressed, unavailable and not-applicable values remain NoData, and registered residents omit commuters, patients, pupils, rail passengers, responders and visitors.

evidenceSources.title: Omgevingsvisie Heiloo 2040, water nuisance and climate-adaptation pages
evidenceSources.edition: Public planning documents and current municipal pages inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The official vision identifies relatively large areas with flood danger, significant heavy-rain nuisance east of the strandwal and over much of northern Heiloo, heat in hardened northern-edge and south-western areas and climate-related nature/fire risk.

Municipal water pages state that extreme rainfall can exceed sewer and surface-water capacity, distinguish municipal rain/sewer/groundwater duties from HHNK surface-water/dike and PWN drinking-water/dune duties, and document separated sewers and local storage measures.

The municipal material is authoritative dated risk and project context, not a live event, reusable calibrated depth raster, operational sewer state, probability or restoration commitment. The PDF/page family does not provide one verified machine update cadence, complete NoData contract or blanket data licence.

evidenceSources.title: Water-retaining roads, Stationsweg-Zeeweg and Zuiderloo water-system projects
evidenceSources.edition: Project pages current 3 September 2026; Stationsweg-Zeeweg works planned March 2025 through late 2026
supports: Official pages identify water nuisance at particular streets and water-retaining road/separated storm-sewer measures at Westerweg, Kerkelaan, Belieslaan, Stationsweg, Zeeweg and Heerenweg.

The Stationsweg-Zeeweg project includes a drainage transport sewer, lowered green strips and road storage but was still scheduled through late 2026; the works must not be assumed complete without commissioning evidence.

Zuiderloo's ditch structure is explicitly not yet complete or at full strength and uses a temporary connection to the polder sewer in north-east Zuiderloo. Project state is dated context, not proof of event-time capacity or protection.
No page supplies full catchment topology, inlet/culvert state, compatible capacity units, pump telemetry, event depth, uncertainty, NoData or a reusable causal licence.

evidenceSources.title: LIWO flood-scenario catalogue and HHNK regional water-system context
evidenceSources.edition: LIWO release 2025.1.6; official pages and public services inspected 3 September 2026
supports: LIWO 2025.1.6 is an expert scenario catalogue, not a live forecast. The nearest primary candidate found in a local bounding box is STRAND_DUIN_KM_37.5 west of the Heiloo boundary; a bounding-box match must not be assigned to GM0399.

Point-in-polygon review finds eighteen regional catalogue candidates inside GM0399: eight Egmondervaart, six Hoevervaart and four Uitwatering van de Baafjespolder points. Candidate existence is not a selected breach, event, condition, probability, depth or affected footprint.

HHNK describes the wider low-lying Sammerspolder system as a vulnerable bowl between dunes and higher Bergen/Heiloo, pumped toward the Schermerboezem through a constrained Alkmaar system. This is regional pathway context, not proof that a particular footprint intersects Heiloo or is active.

A causal adapter must preserve catalogue release, model/scenario date, source water, defence/breach/variant, native CRS/resolution/units, coverage, NoData, depth/velocity/arrival/duration/recession, uncertainty, licence and expert approval. The exact LIWO product licence for a selected layer must be verified before redistribution.

evidenceSources.title: TOP10NL woodland and regional nature-fire context
evidenceSources.edition: TOP10NL feature inspected 3 September 2026; source actuality 1 January 2018 and registration 1 April 2020
supports: A point at the official Gemeentebos neighbourhood centre intersects TOP10NL feature 3a17122b-2f4e-5cf9-b571-a70610a6e3e0, classified bos: loofbos, with aerial-photo source, 0.1 accuracy and old 2018/2020 validity metadata. TOP10NL is generally CC BY 4.0.

The public IPO fire dataset returns no source-holder Heiloo feature in the inspected local bounding box; nearby records belong to Bergen/Castricum. No local match is Unknown/coverage-limited, not evidence of no combustible vegetation or no fire risk.

VRNHN describes nature-fire risk in the regional coast/dune zone. Static land-cover and risk-object evidence can establish dated eligibility only, never current fuel/moisture, ignition, perimeter, wind/smoke, firewater, access or suppression state.

evidenceSources.title: IMWA/DAMO water-control and wastewater asset snapshot for GM0399
evidenceSources.edition: Public national aggregation snapshot retrieved 3 September 2026
supports: The CC BY-SA 4.0 public deployment assigns 65 point assets to GM0399 by full 2025 boundary containment: 50 weirs, twelve surface-water pumps, two sewer pumps and RWZI Heiloo.

Named records include Heiloo-Oost, Groot-Limmerpolder Noord, Baafjespolder, De Leije, Kanaalweg, Ypestein, Varnebroekmolen, Rg RWZI Heiloo and Rg Boekelermeerweg. These establish registered asset presence and class only.

Registered capacity fields cannot be assumed to share units or measure current usable throughput; a value of zero is a recorded value but is not proof that an asset is retired without field semantics. Points do not prove topology, direction, telemetry, operation, power/backup, condition, staffing or restoration.

evidenceSources.publisher: Rijkswaterstaat / ProRail / OVapi / NDW / Gemeente Heiloo
evidenceSources.title: NWB roads, Heiloo station and stops, current situations and Heilooerbos crossings
evidenceSources.edition: NWB-Light 1 August 2026; GTFS version 9543; public records inspected 2-3 September 2026
supports: The CC0 monthly NWB-derived logical graph has three GM0399 edges: A9 north to Alkmaar, A9 south to Castricum and a short N203 connection to Castricum, with nominal scenario capacities 260/260/150. These are simplified proxies, not verified emergency throughput.

ProRail's manually updated CC0 register identifies Heiloo station and GTFS version 9543 identifies twenty stop areas including Station, GGZ-Gezondheidscentrum and Onze Lieve Vrouwe ter Nood. Static geometry and schedules do not establish passengers, accessibility, service, evacuation throughput or restoration.

The municipality documents three unprotected crossings in Landgoed Nijenburg/Heilooërbos and planned changes including closure/transformation and a footbridge. Planning text must retain valid state; it is not proof that works are complete or a crossing is open.
The CC0 NDW snapshot assigns zero covered current situations to GM0399. This means no matching covered report at publication time, never that A9, N203, local roads, railway or crossings are open.

evidenceSources.title: Acute-care availability near Heiloo and Landgoed Willibrordus forensic-care context
evidenceSources.edition: RIVM acute care v1.1 published 3 July 2026; GGZ public pages inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The CC0 RIVM questionnaire assigns zero covered acute-care locations inside GM0399. Noordwest Ziekenhuisgroep Alkmaar is approximately 3.408 km straight-line from the municipal centre and reports a 24/7 emergency department and acute obstetrics, 28 treatment rooms and 31,080 visits in 2025.
Questionnaire facts are dated facility context, not event-time route, occupancy, acceptance, staffing, supplies, backup or usable capacity. Straight-line distance is not a patient-transfer route.

GGZ NHN identifies forensic-care clinics at Landgoed Willibrordus and describes two forensic sites with 64 places. Exact current occupancy, dependency, evacuation suitability, staff, medicines and backup are not public operational state.
A new HIC with 60 planned places was described as construction in 2025/2026 with expected completion late 2026. Planned capacity must not be counted as operating unless commissioning is confirmed.

evidenceSources.publisher: Netbeheer Nederland / Partners in Energie; RDI; DUO
evidenceSources.title: Electricity planning sample, antenna installations and education locations
supports: One postcode sample at 1851LB identifies Liander station Heiloo 10-1i + 10-2i, withdrawal queue 2.9 MW/21 requests, injection queue 21 MW/14 requests, TenneT classes 3/3, 33 projects and earliest project year 2026. Existing/required values are null. This is planning context, not full network coverage, topology, live load, outage or restoration; the exact dataset licence identifier was not found.

RDI's public register assigns 31 installations to GM0399: sixteen mobile, seven fixed-link, six amateur and two broadcast records. Its exact reuse licence and service cadence were not established; records do not prove coverage, traffic, backhaul, power/backup or availability.

DUO identifies fifteen education-use locations under CC BY, with deployment version not established in this audit. Registered use does not establish people present, shelter designation, supplies, generator endurance, accessibility or live operation.

evidenceSources.title: First-three-days preparation, regional risk governance and crisis plan
evidenceSources.edition: Municipal page and Regionaal Crisisplan 2025 inspected 3 September 2026
supports: Heiloo tells residents to prepare for the first three days, describes municipal reception when evacuation is ordered and alternatives are unavailable, and identifies crisis communication/nazorg and regional radio 88.9. This does not prove a shelter is activated, stocked, accessible or staffed.

VRNHN's public 2024-2027 policy identifies extreme weather/flooding, prolonged electricity interruption and infectious threats as priorities. Meeting records stated that the 2022 regional risk profile update was delayed for new methodology; no later machine-valid event model was established here.

The officially published Regionaal Crisisplan 2025 establishes governance but not a live incident, warning, resource inventory, route, reception place, decision or restoration state. Public narrative pages have no single machine refresh/coverage/NoData contract or confirmed blanket licence.

findings.summary: Generic coastal proximity becomes precise inland Heiloo flood and service impact without a selected LIWO/HHNK hydraulic event.
findings.evidence: At coastal T+24 the model reports internal flood field 2.552973, 13,329 affected people-equivalent and drainage availability 0.203148. findings.action: Retain coastal proximity only as a hidden non-operational diagnostic and suppress decision-facing depth, neighbourhood impact, affected people and direct service loss until an expert-selected, versioned LIWO/HHNK event carries source water, defence/breach/variant, footprint, depth/velocity/arrival/duration/recession, CRS/resolution/units/NoData, uncertainty, licence and approval. Retain river zero solely as a narrowly labelled named-major-river result; regional water, groundwater, sewer and pluvial paths remain Unknown.

residualLimitations: This is a deterministic first-72-hour planning stress test, not a KNMI, WMCN/LIWO, HHNK, VRNHN, municipality or operator warning, forecast, probability, evacuation order, casualty model or restoration commitment.

No expert-selected Heiloo North Sea/dune, regional-water, polder, groundwater, sewer or pluvial scenario, defence/breach/overtopping state, connected footprint, arrival, velocity, duration/recession, verified units or NoData mask drives the simulation.
The exact-zero river result applies only to direct Rhine/Meuse/IJssel forcing; Egmondervaart, Hoevervaart, Baafjespolder, boezem, regional-kade, groundwater, sewer and pluvial risk remains Unknown.

LIWO catalogue candidate points, including eighteen within the boundary, are not selected events, probabilities, breaches or depth footprints; bounding-box candidates outside GM0399 must not be assigned.

Municipal climate/project pages are dated context. Stationsweg-Zeeweg continuing through late 2026 and temporary/incomplete Zuiderloo works must not be represented as completed protection without commissioning evidence.
CBS generalized polygons and label points do not resolve terrain, water compartments, sewers, buildings, paving, shade, fuels, care sites, corridors or household exposure.
CBS fields are rounded/suppressed; district-heating and charging are absent everywhere and other fields are sparse. Null is Unknown, never zero service, demand or safety.
Registered residents omit commuters, patients, staff, station passengers, pupils, visitors, responders and recreational users; no authorized event-time transient occupancy ledger is available.

TOP10NL Gemeentebos land cover is old static eligibility only; no live fuel, moisture, ignition, perimeter, wind, access, firewater or suppression state is available, and no IPO Heiloo match is not evidence of safety.
Static NWB, ProRail and GTFS geometry/schedules do not establish live A9/N203/local-road, crossing, rail, bus, evacuation, emergency-priority or freight state and capacity.
Zero covered NDW situations is no covered report at publication time, not proof that roads, rail or crossings are open; crossing project plans must retain their date/state.

IMWA/DAMO points do not establish full hydraulic/wastewater topology, compatible capacity units, control logic, current operation, power backup, crews or repair. A zero capacity field needs its source semantics and is not automatically retired.

No complete public physical Liander feeder/switching, PWN pipe/pressure/quality, gas district/valve, telecom backhaul or municipal sewer topology is authorized in the model; the postcode sample is planning context only.

No RIVM acute-care respondent inside GM0399 is a coverage fact, not zero care need. External hospital acceptance/access, GGZ occupancy, staffing, medicines, generators and patient transfer remain Unknown.
Planned 60-place HIC capacity must not be counted as operational without commissioning evidence; the reported 64 forensic places do not provide live occupancy or evacuation readiness.
Education and antenna records identify registered installation/use, not shelter activation, people present, coverage, backhaul, capacity, backup or recovery.
Cyber disruption has no named target, architecture, attack/detection/containment state or authoritative operational evidence; generic loss is not an observed incident.
No validated inventory is available for reception/shelters, pumps/generators, fuel, food/water/medicine stocks, crews, vehicles, mutual aid, household preparedness or completed actions.

Event-attributable essential-service person-hours is a matched-no-event weighted availability proxy, not customer outage-hours, injuries, mortality, evacuation, displacement or welfare loss; 72 hours excludes prolonged contamination and reconstruction.
